name: PtrHash (author benchmark blog)
workload: Query throughput and construction time for a minimal perfect hash function over 300 million string keys and 10^9 integer keys, single machine, multi-threaded construction.
claimed_speedup: PtrHash Fast: 33 ns/query (loop), 16 ns/query (streaming), 27 ns/key construction (6 threads), 2.99 bits/key; PtrHash Default: 37/23 ns/query, 32 ns/key construction, 2.40 bits/key; vs PTHash-CC 77 ns/query and PHOBIC 108-179 ns/query; ~8 ns/key streaming query on 10^9 integer keys, 'just short of the 7.4 ns inverse throughput of random memory access' (verbatim from author's blog)
hardware: Intel Core i7-10750H, 6 cores, 2.6 GHz, DDR4-3200
tradeoffs: Rust implementation (usable from C via FFI, not a native C++ library); numbers are self-reported by the author on their own blog, matching the companion SEA 2025 paper.
caveats: This is a first-party author blog post (not independent), and exact compiler flags for the reported numbers were not stated on the page, so capped at Tier B even though the underlying repo and a peer-reviewed paper (SEA 2025) exist. ptrhash's canonical repo is already on the KNOWN_LIST, so this is reported only as additional evidence for a known project.
found_via: Blogs / talks: web search 'minimal perfect hash function benchmark blog comparison BBHash PTHash' surfaced 'PtrHash: Minimal Perfect Hashing at RAM Throughput · CuriousCoding' (author's own engineering blog), opened and verified directly.

name: frozen (serge-sans-paille/frozen) -- new benchmark evidence
workload: Same three demos as the static_maps paper (element-mass, codon, and stock-symbol lookup), run independently by the static_maps authors against both frozen::unordered_map and std::unordered_map on identical hardware/compiler/build
claimed_speedup: (derived from page data) frozen::unordered_map's average runtime is roughly 50% of std::unordered_map on the elements demo (44.9 vs 89.6 microsec avg), roughly 78% on the codon demo (1365.5 vs 1746.8 microsec avg), and roughly 74% on the stocks demo (15804.5 vs 21228.1 microsec avg), computed by comparing the paper's separate frozen-vs-static_maps and std-vs-static_maps panels for the same demo
tradeoffs: Already catalogued elsewhere (frozen is on the KNOWN_LIST); this record exists solely to capture fresh, independent Tier A benchmark evidence for it found via arXiv this session
caveats: The std-vs-frozen ratio is derived by combining two separate comparison panels from the same figure/paper (each directly measured against static_maps on the same demo/hardware/compiler) rather than a single head-to-head frozen-vs-std run; frozen also has a notably higher compile time on the stock demo (21.1s vs 1.5s for std::unordered_map) due to constexpr overhead
found_via: arXiv export API query search_query=abs:"perfect hash" AND abs:"unordered_map" (paper arXiv:2602.22506)
